knowHow.text: high dimensional accuracy of the printed elements
high surface quality after printing
In addition, the glass fibres give the prints a distinctive texture, which, in addition to its undoubted aesthetic qualities, also translates into increased usability.
Thanks to its extremely high interlayer adhesion and low shrinkage, it allows even intermediate users to execute large prints.
Dry box not necessary
Ruby or hardened nozzle recommended
Making tooling, equipment, and manufacturing aids.
This makes glass fiber reinforced filaments perfect for 3D printing applications that require mechanical strength and stiffness.
No enclosure, or heated chamber needed.
This engineering filament is very easy to 3D print on open desktop machines.
Your 3D printed parts will not only be stiff, strong and durable.
They will also be resistant to wear and chemicals.
Durable and good resistance to corrosion.
It offers not only great electrical- and thermal insulation properties.
Reducing shrinkage / warping
Increasing dimensional stability
Its low shrinkage factor and perfect layer adhesion make AthenaX GF10 a breeze to print with.
Masking layer lines with a matt surface finish in 3D printed objects
We recommend to use ruby nozzles or hardened steel nozzles.
Please be aware that glass fiber reinforced filaments contain a relatively high concentration of extremely hard glass fibers, which have an abrasive nature.
In general these glass fibers will accelerate the nozzle-wear of brass nozzles, much faster than unfilled filaments.
PCTG is moderately hygroscopic and therefore it is recommended to pre-dry the filament at 75°C for approximately 24 hours before usage for optimal results.
For optimal print results we recommend to print AthenaX GF10 filament from a drying box to avoid that the material can accumulate humidity from the environment.
it retains its key advantages: chemical resistance, low shrinkage, and ease of printing
The result is a material with increased strength, stiffness, and impact resistance
